extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and practitioners (patent owners, requesters, patent attorneys/agents) involved in ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for the form and content of Office actions in ex parte reexamination proceedings, specifying what must be included in first and subsequent actions, procedural steps (panel review, signatures), handling of requester/patent-owner submissions, and title/amendment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of first Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s first Office action will be a statement of the examiner’s position and should be so complete that the second Office action can properly be made a final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first Office action should set out the examiner's position thoroughly (see MPEP §2271) so that follow-on actions may be final; prepare detailed explanation and reasoning in the first action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detail required for stating rejections (pertinency and manner of applying prior art)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first Office action must be sufficiently detailed that the pertinency and manner of applying the cited prior art to the claims in each rejection is clearly set forth therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly explain why cited patents/printed publications are pertinent and precisely how they are applied to each claim; show mapping between prior art and claim limitations so the rejection is understandable and defensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation and review of requester-supplied materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the request for reexamination includes material such as a claim chart to explain a proposed rejection, the examiner may bodily incorporate the claim chart (or other material) within the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If incorporating requester materials, the examiner must carefully review them to ensure any items incorporated in a statement of the rejection clearly and completely address the patentability of the claims; do not blindly adopt requester charts without verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing patent owner responses in subsequent actions
rubrics_metrics.description: For actions subsequent to the first Office action, the examiner must be careful to additionally address all patent owner responses to previous actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent Office actions should explicitly respond to the substance of patent owner amendments and arguments from earlier rounds; ensure each prior response is considered and explained in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explaining reasons for patentability or allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner concludes in any Office action that one or more of the claims are patentable over the cited patents or printed publications, the examiner should indicate why the claim(s) is/are clearly patentable in a manner similar to that used to indicate reasons for allowance (MPEP §1302.14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When finding claims patentable, provide clear reasons and supporting references (or point to record portions that establish patentability) analogous to allowance explanations so the basis for patentability is on the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to arguments under relevant CFR provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The first action should also respond to the substance of each argument raised by the patent owner and requester pursuant to 37 CFR 1.510, 1.530, and 1.535. If arguments are presented which are inappropriate in reexamination, they should be treated in accordance with 37 CFR 1.552(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the Office action replies to each substantive argument raised under the cited CFR sections; identify and treat inappropriate or noncompliant arguments according to the specified regulation (1.552(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of patent owner statements (37 CFR 1.501(a)(2)) when relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: If any statement of the patent owner submitted pursuant to 37 CFR 1.501(a)(2) is relied upon in the detailed explanation, requester must have explained how that statement is being used to determine the proper meaning of a patent claim in connection with prior art applied to that claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When examiner relies on a patent-owner statement, check that requester provided an explanation of how that statement informs claim meaning relative to applied prior art; that explanation will be considered in drafting the Office action and in determining claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughness because of finality of reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: It is especially important that the examiner’s action in reexamination be thorough and complete in view of the finality of a reexamination proceeding and the patent owner’s inability to file a continuation proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the heightened importance of exhaustive examination and clear record-making in reexamination due to the proceeding's finality and limited procedural remedies for the patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title change procedures and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally, the title will not need to be changed during reexamination. If a change of the title is necessary, patent owner should be notified of the need to provide an amendment changing the title as early as possible in the prosecution as a part of an Office Action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all claims are found patentable and a Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) has been or is to be mailed, a change to the title by the examiner may only be done by a formal Examiner’s Amendment; changing the title and merely initialing the change is NOT permitted in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews, discussions, and amendment handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Current procedure permits the examiner, in the exercise of professional judgment, to indicate that a discussion with the patent owner’s representative may result in agreement whereby the reexamination proceeding may be placed in condition for issuing a Notice of Intent to Issue a Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) and that the examiner will contact the patent owner’s representative within about two weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment resulting from such discussions may be made by the patent owner’s attorney/agent or by the examiner in an examiner’s amendment. When extensive amendments are necessary, it is preferable that the patent owner file them, because that provides a better file wrapper record including the patent owner’s arguments for patentability as required by 37 CFR 1.111.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review conference and signature/initialing procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a patent owner response to the action by the CRU, or upon the expiration of the time to submit the response, the examiner will be notified. The examiner will prepare for and set up a panel review conference as per MPEP §2271.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may prepare the Office action before or after the conference and revise as needed. If the conference confirms the preliminary decision to reject and/or allow the claims, the Office action shall be issued and signed by the examiner, with two or more other conferees initialing the action (as 'conferee') to indicate their presence in the conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standard transmittal/form and structured headings
rubrics_metrics.description: A sample of a first Office action in a reexamination proceeding is set forth below. Form PTOL-465, Ex Parte Reexamination Communication Transmittal Form, is used and standardized section headings (e.g., 2201 Introduction; 2202 Citation of Prior Art and Written Statements; ... 2262 Form and Content of Office Action; etc.) are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the sample/form structure (PTOL-465) and the prescribed section headings and organization when preparing and transmitting the Office action to ensure consistency and completeness.
